title: Gas rates, public art and dog designation changes
subtitle: Heritage demolition notice, RISE equity grants, multiyear procurement, volunteer awards and mayor's 30-year service recognition.
overview: Council approved Kitchener Utilities' natural gas delivery rates for all Kitchener customers, effective January 1, 2026 {{vote:m8}}. It also approved improvements to the dog designation process {{vote:m9}} and a new public artwork, "The Seams," for Upper Canada Park as part of the final phase of facility improvements {{vote:m6}}.

Other decisions included endorsing revisions to the RISE grant framework for equity-denied communities {{vote:m7}}, approving the external audit plan for 2025 {{vote:m2}}, and allowing multiyear non-standard procurement agreements of up to five years {{vote:m10}}. On heritage, Council let the notice period run on a demolition notice for 11 Irvin Street and directed that the property be photographed first {{vote:m4}}. It also corrected the description of a property designation to cover only part of 2219 Ottawa Street South {{vote:m11}}.

The meeting opened with recognitions: the Mayor's 30 years of elected service, the Kitchener Blues Festival's 25th anniversary, and long-service awards for sports groups, neighbourhood associations and advisory committee volunteers. In his update, the Mayor reported that weekend GO Train service to Kitchener is set to start November 23.

decisions.detail: Council approved Kitchener Utilities' proposed variable and fixed natural gas delivery rates for all Kitchener delivery customers, effective January 1, 2026.
Council approved the improvements to the dog designation process outlined in staff report CSD-2025-381.
Council approved commissioning the artwork "The Seams" for Upper Canada Park and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign an agreement with the artist team.
Council endorsed revisions to the Racialized and Indigenous Supports for Equity grant framework to match the evolving needs of equity-denied communities.
Council approved non-standard procurement and agreements of up to five years with the suppliers listed in the staff report attachment.
Council received the notice of intention to demolish as information, let the notice period run its course, and directed that the property be photographed before any demolition.
Council amended its August resolution to remove 808 Bleams Road and limit the intended heritage designation to a described part of 2219 Ottawa Street South.
Council approved the audit planning report for the year ended December 31, 2025, prepared by KPMG.

debate: The transcript records no debate on the motions. Each was moved, put to a vote without discussion, and carried.
A delegate from Sustainable Waterloo Region said the regional greenhouse gas inventory showed a 12% reduction but that the region is still not on track to meet its 2030 targets.

The same delegate described the organization's work as largely practical: insulation, windows, more efficient manufacturing and culture change. The delegate argued that sustainability is good business because an efficient business is a sustainable one.

In response to a councillor's question, the delegate said businesses that commit to sustainability often become more innovative and prosperous over the long term. Other councillors thanked the organization for its work.
